program: Expected ordinary-gift health conditional on explicit case-mix assumptions

nutshell.headline: The omitted specialties materially raise estimated health, but the result remains uncertain and expensive.
nutshell.body: For $100,000, central net health is 0.513674 QALYs nationally. Donor cost per10Q is $1,946,762 US, $3,244,603 Bay and $24,334,519 SF. These are conditional case-mix expectations, not measured OA outcomes.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Coordinated donated specialty treatment can relieve persistent bleeding, neuropathy, obstruction, pain and vision loss across multiple specialties.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Current specialty totals are known but modern diagnosis frequencies are not. Historical mix, heterogeneous trial comparators, generic utility mapping and no-gift timing require explicit priors.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No verified marginal procedure mix, distinct-patient wait comparison or complete treatment linkage. Even joint favorable national donor scenario is about$465k/10Q.

summary.label: Full gift
summary.detail: All-function coordination cost retained across all10 specialty categories; no inverse allocation uplift.

summary.label: Gross associated resources
summary.detail: All nominal service clinical/support/time resources retained, plus explicit further-treatment allowance; not waived charges or net societal costs.

programSection.body: Recipient Ambulatory Surgery Access Coalition dba Operation Access, EIN94-3180356, coordinates donated outpatient specialty services for eligible uninsured people.2025reported1,529services across10specialties; these are not distinct patients or diagnosis-specific procedures.

steps.title: Allocate current specialty service equivalents
steps.detail: Use complete whole-gift cash and existing specialty costs; no repeated overhead or navigation multiplier.

steps.title: Use a complete named case-mix ledger
steps.detail: Each specialty sums to100%across old and new pathways, with fractions explicitly assumed rather than observed.

steps.title: Count finite earlier appropriate treatment
steps.detail: Symptom relief stops with comparator catch-up, recurrence, death or horizon. Diagnosis requires management; acute harm remains.

programSection.boundary: Current specialties are verified, but naming a representative diagnosis does not establish actual OA procedure frequency. Expected organization health is conditional on the inspectable case-mix prior. Other assessment2%has explicitzero benefit plus burden.

model.headline: Named-pathway coverage replaces the three-subset headline
model.body: Preserves original finite CRC, cataract and hernia components; adds21named clinical/assessment rows. No generic residual QALY-per-dollar parameter.

equation.label: Each new clinical row
equation.expression: People=whole gift×specialty allocation/cost×diagnostic share×common additional-activity factor÷services/episode×disjoint fraction. Q=people×[success/linkage×signed utility gain×delay discount×finite annuity(catch-up+recurrence+death+discount,H)−acute burden]. Sum all rows and original components; retain whole gift and all nominal clinical resources.
equation.result: Central 0.5136735945144643 QALYs; same full gift priced against each geographic share.

inputs.label: crc annual fatal hazard reduction
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios

inputs.label: crc baseline total mortality hazard
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios

inputs.label: crc catchup hazard
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios
inputs.basis: .5/year aggregate hazard-effect decay prior (two-year characteristic time) for eventual ordinary diagnostic/treatment care; mean-hazard approximation, not exact random individual care-time mixture.

inputs.label: crc latency years
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios
inputs.basis: Two-year assumed lag from procedure to differential fatal risk. Not observed OA survival timing; existing alternative care can catch up during this lag.

inputs.label: crc active years
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios
inputs.basis: Five years of possibly different fatal hazard after latency, not five avoided deaths or a life expectancy.

inputs.label: crc horizon years
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios
inputs.basis: Ten-year finite survival observation from procedure; both arms return to common mortality after the hazard-effect window. No lifetime tail.

inputs.label: crc delay years
inputs.range: Existing bounded foundation model and v2 scenarios
inputs.basis: Quarter-year procedure delay; cohort already conditioned alive at service start, so delay discounts only.

model.fundingBoundary: Current cash-like expense and all-service donated clinical resources are retained from the audited foundation. No additional slots or restricted offer is verified. New health does not add duplicate hospital costs; six follow-on diagnostic/treatment rows add$200per nominal service. Gross associated resources are not net induced costs, and no public reimbursement or waived-charge saving is subtracted.
model.uncertaintyBoundary: Within-specialty diagnosis mix is not measured. This is a conditional expected whole-organization model, not a confidence interval or claim that all named procedures are currently supplied at these frequencies.

evidence.design: Current annual report plus historical descriptive study
evidence.population: OA specialty services, not unique diagnosis cohorts
evidence.result: Current10specialty totals anchor resource allocation; historical within-general-surgery mix informs weak priors only.
evidence.transfer: Postprocedure yes/no surveys are not utility scores; actual treated waits are not counterfactual waits avoided.

evidence.design: Randomized surgery vs conservative/medical care trials
evidence.population: Confirmed CTS and refractory abnormal uterine bleeding
evidence.result: CTS utility difference at12months was small/nonsignificant; AUB earlier benefit diminished as comparator patients received surgery.
evidence.transfer: No integrated-QALY misreading, no ablation-vs-hysterectomy comparison substituted for access.

evidence.design: TURP, septoplasty, veins, foot and other primary trials
evidence.population: Selected symptomatic patients with organ-specific comparators
evidence.result: Some procedures improve symptoms; C-GALL/degenerative-knee evidence cautions against generic surgical benefits.
evidence.transfer: Utility gains, success and diagnosis mix remain explicit priors. No one specialty's efficacy is assigned unchanged to another.

reservations: Case-mix hypotheses cover all material specialties but current diagnosis crosswalk is missing.
Medical, splint, pessary and later-surgery alternatives prevent interpreting treatment as lifelong benefit versus no care.
New named pathways increase central health roughlyeightfold; v1three-subset headline was not a whole-organization expected return.
Some pathways have weak primary causal evidence and explicit utility priors; linked diagnostic benefit and severe cancer outcomes remain especially uncertain.
excludedBenefits: Repeated full-person health for multiple services or specialties
Money/waived charges or work-productivity gains converted into QALYs
Lifetime symptom benefit after comparator care, recurrence or death
Unestablished benefit of the2%other-assessment category; burden retained
